newsitem.title: USA: Columbus Energy puzzled by stock weakness.
newsitem.headline: Columbus Energy puzzled by stock weakness.

text.p: Columbus Energy Corp said on Monday it could not account for the recent weakness in its share price and it expected to meet forecasts for fiscal 1996 results.
The company expected its discretionary cash flow would at least equal and could surpass management's previous forecast of $6.2 million, or $2 per share, for this fiscal year.

Columbus should also report net earnings for fiscal 1996 of about $0.60 per share, compared with a loss in 1995 of $1.5 million, or $0.48 per share, after a $3.06 million non-cash "impairment of long-lived asset" charge, the company said.

Columbus also said it expected oil and gas sales in 1996, from U.S. properties alone, would be about $10.5 million, up from $7.9 million in fiscal 1995. Last year's data also included $639,000 of sales from its former Canadian unit which was divested in February 1995.
